part: Jordan brings Happy back while Tony is away
where: description, example, how (steps 2 to 4 and the rehearsal), value, wave
problem: The card is scored 4 and placed in wave A on two things nobody has said: that Tony is away overnight often enough for a power cut to matter, and that Jordan is willing to type a disk password and run Terminal commands at the Mac. part: browser action firewall hook: profile, target and node pin, URL and nested-request parsing, kind-mismatch check, and the host-browser fallback they guard
problem: Most of the hook repeats limits that config already sets for a browser in the sandbox container, or parses fields for rules this build does not have: there is no site allowlist, and every click-and-type action is already blocked by name. The pins matter only if the browser runs on the host instead, which the roadmap's own exit test and the vendor's advice both steer away from. It is in-house code on the security boundary that needs a contract test after every OpenClaw update.
checked: Roadmap lines 111 and 271 (the browser lives in its own container with the LAN blocked; the M3 exit test is 'browser cannot reach the LAN'), line 401 (research holds no private data), line 432 (approval before form interaction and no submit apply to the jobs agent only), lines 267 and 270 ('links, not bookings'; no booking capability on the schedule) and the fact sheet's never list (CAPTCHA solving). Installed docs/tools/browser/agent-tools.md line 39 and docs/gateway/sandboxing/docker-backend.md line 91 (a sandboxed session cannot target the host browser; allowHostControl defaults to false). Installed type definitions (dist/runtime-api-Bw-xbtMx.d.ts line 41557): the tool has 24 actions, and besides `act` and `upload` they include `download`, `dialog`, `emulate` and `importprofile`. Card text: 'there is no site allowlist here' and `act` 'blocks every act kind at once'.

proposal.text: Keep read-only in code, because a browser that can click and type could fill a public booking form or tick a CAPTCHA box, and both are on the never list. But make the hook one rule: a short allowlist of action names for the research agent (the read-only subset the card already lists), everything else blocked, failing closed. An allowlist, not a two-name block list, so that an action added by an update stays blocked. Drop the profile, target and node pin, the URL reading, the nested-request parsing and the kind-mismatch check. Use the sandbox browser container only, with allowHostControl left false and evaluateEnabled false in config; if the image cannot be built, F020 waits, with no host-browser fallback.

loses: A second, in-house copy of limits that config already sets, and the option of running the browser on the host. If scrolling or hovering is ever allowed back, the nested-request check has to be written then.
challenge_note: The never list (bookings, CAPTCHA) is a real reason to keep clicking and typing blocked in code, so I repaired the proposal from a two-name block list to an action-name allowlist; the pins and the parsing serve no rule once the browser is the sandbox container, so that part of the finding stands.

None has come from the family, the card calls its volume numbers design numbers and names no hours or rooms, and as written, quiet hours on the Hue plugin could refuse 'lights off' at bedtime, which is the card's own example.
checked: Card unverified point 4 ('The volume caps (35, and 10 at night) are design numbers, not sourced'). Fact sheet (quiet hours and preferred times never stated; family.json5 records no rooms or routines). The 9 Oct scan shows two speakers. No roadmap rule covers house devices, and the notification policy's quiet hours (G001) are about unprompted texts, not a parent's own command. In the card's design no timed job is given these tools, so nothing switches at night unless a parent is texting.

proposal.text: Only if Tony said yes to switching: keep one hard volume cap in the Sonos plugin, the one limit that bounds harm from a wrong or injected command, and ask Tony for that one number (default: the card's 35, marked as a starting value). Drop quiet hours and the night cap for on-request commands, and add a room allowlist only when there is a room to leave out.

loses: A code block against lights or music being switched late at night by mistake.
challenge_note: I looked for a roadmap rule or a stated preference behind the three limits and found none; this row merges the over-engineering row with the assumption row on the unsourced numbers.

part: the 22:30 goodnight check text and who receives it
problem: The description states a 22:30 text as fact and says 'a parent' gets it. Tony has given no time of day, no quiet hours and no recipient, the notification policy may drop a text that late, and the card says the Hue app can already switch lights at a set time.
checked: Card caveats 4 and 14 and its last dependency ('22:30 is a house choice, not a fixed part of the design'). Fact sheet (preferred times and quiet hours never stated). G001 description (a text outside the allowed hours is dropped, and those hours are not set yet). Card unverified point 7 (the two tools are not installed and their output was never parsed).

proposal.text: Would a text when lights or speakers are still on at night be useful, or is a lights-off time set in the Hue app enough? Default: leave the check out and set the time in the Hue app. If yes: at what time, and to you, to Jordan or to both; the description then reads 'at a time Tony sets'.

loses: A nightly nudge that also covers the speakers.
challenge_note: I checked the card and the fact sheet for a chosen time or recipient and found the card itself calling 22:30 a house choice; the two reviewers' rows are merged, with the more cautious default.

part: printing through Happy at all, and 'the home printer' being the Canon PRO-100 the scan saw

checked: Fact sheet ('Known from a scan, not from Tony'; the scan saw a Canon PRO-100). frame.decisions (none gates F080). challenge_note: I repeated the search and the fetch: the printer's type still rests on a search summary because Canon refuses direct fetches, which is one more reason this is a question for Tony; the two reviewers' rows are merged and the severity lowered to match a card scored 2.

part: scheduled Sunday fridge sheet with its own data reads and a chore rota
where: description, example, how (part 1), depends_on, unverified, demand
problem: The card's lead feature prints a sheet by itself every Sunday with the week's events and 'chore turns'. It needs its own renderer, its own calendar and database reads outside any agent, and a chore rota that has no table, no tool and no known family behind it, and it repeats on paper what the Sunday week-ahead text already sends.
checked: F014 in r7.json (Sunday 18:00 week-ahead brief from the same calendar). Card unverified points 4 and 5 (the script's data reads were not tried; the rota 'was never specified'). removed.json: the chore rota F039 was removed as advised-against and HOM-14 was folded in. Fact sheet: the config repo records no children, chores or routines, and which calendar the family shares is never stated. The card's demand source is general advice about chore charts and 'says nothing about a posted calendar'.

proposal.text: Do you want a page printed by itself every Sunday, and does the family keep a chore rota? Default: no. Drop the automatic sheet and the chore turns; the Sunday week-ahead text (F014) carries the week. If a paper copy is wanted once that text has run for a while, and printing is kept at all, 'print the week' on request sends the same text to the printer.

loses: The automatic page on the fridge each Sunday, the chore turns, and the guarantee that no model wrote what is printed.
challenge_note: I checked the removal log and the fact sheet: the rota comes from an item removed as advised-against and no chores or children are on record; the over-engineering row and the assumption row are merged.

part: 'print this' downloading a link by itself
problem: To print a link, the plugin fetches an address from the host, which the card itself calls a way out for an agent that holds memory. That needs three in-house checks that do not exist yet, for a case a parent can cover by attaching the file.
checked:
Card safety text ('a way out for an agent that holds memory and reads search results'; 'design requirements to build and test, not existing features') and unverified point 2. Roadmap lines 397 and 400:

-main holds memory and reads search results, so it is the agent that must not gain a new way to send data out; dropping the download removes one. Card description ('A phone on the home Wi-Fi can already print by itself').

proposal.text: If printing is kept: 'print this' takes an attached PDF or photo only, which is already on the Mac through F002. No link download. A parent who has a link saves the file on the phone and attaches it.

loses: Printing straight from a pasted link.
challenge_note: I checked the simpler design against the trifecta rule: it removes a way out from the agent that holds memory, so it tightens the hard rule and the finding stands.

part: 'Canon's spec sheet for the PIXMA PRO-100 lists AirPrint'
problem: The card says Canon's spec sheet lists AirPrint and uses that twice: to say phones can already print by themselves, and to expect a driverless print queue to work. No Canon page is among the card's sources, and the card's own AirPrint source note says 'whether this printer is one was not confirmed'.
checked: Card sources (no canon.com entry; the Apple AirPrint entry says the printer was not confirmed). Card 'adds' ('Whether this printer supports AirPrint from the phones is unconfirmed'). A search of Canon's and Apple's sites in this run suggests the model supports AirPrint, but no first-party page could be opened (Canon returned HTTP 403).

proposal.text: Only if printing is kept: from an iPhone on the home Wi-Fi, open any PDF, tap Share and then Print, and see whether the printer appears. Thirty seconds, no build. If it appears, 'print this' matters only away from home; if it does not, the driverless queue is in doubt too. Reword the caveat to say which it was.

loses: nothing
challenge_note: I looked for a first-party page behind the claim and could not open one either, so a thirty-second check on a phone remains the right way to settle it.

checked: Card demand and sources (OpenClaw's system-prompt and standing-intents pages). Card caveat 5. Take AUT-01 out of the waves; the one-shot planner (F028) and plain reminders (F007) cover the rest, and if the wish comes up later, the simpler design in the next row needs no build of its own.

loses: Project check-ins as a named feature.
challenge_note: I looked for a request from Tony or a dependent card and found neither; the only backing is vendor documentation that the mechanism exists.

part: one self-pacing scheduled job per project, with its own tools
problem: The check-in job picks its own gap, reads the note with tools and deletes itself, which needs an exception to the rule that timed jobs carry no tools, on top of a grant the vendor advises against. A fixed 'every three days' reminder gives the same nudge.
checked: Installed docs/automation/cron-jobs/schedules.md line 19 (a plain fixed interval exists) and its pacing section (optional). F007 in r7.json (recurring reminders with an empty tool list, already behind the recipient pin). Card caveats 8 and 9 and its last dependency (the vendor's advice against the grant, and the open tool-list decision). The card's example asks only to 'check in with me every few days'. The simpler design stays inside F007's rule that a timed job carries no tools, so it loosens no hard rule.

proposal.text: No new mechanism. A project is a note in the parent's memory (F041), one ordinary recurring reminder (F007) such as 'Party project: reply status for what is open', and one rule in the agent's instructions for keeping the note. The parent cancels the reminder when the project is done.

loses: The check-in text does not list the open items by itself (the parent replies to get them), Happy does not vary the gap, and the reminder is not removed automatically.
challenge_note: I checked the simpler design against the recipient pin and the empty-tool-list rule in F007: it needs no exception to either, and nothing in the card's sources requires self-pacing.
